reconcile.connective: Harmonizers read Satan's "world rulership" as men's voluntary subjection — a real but derivative, permitted sway — not as ownership rivaling YHWH's sovereignty.

discrepancy.connective: Elaine Pagels argues the obstructive, wholly-subordinate satan of the Hebrew Bible is recast in the New Testament as a cosmic "prince of this world," introducing a near-dualism the older affirmations of YHWH's sole rule do not anticipate.

skeptic.name: Elaine Pagels
skeptic.attribution: Elaine Pagels, The Origin of Satan (1995)

excerpts.excerpt_text: No doubt these passages only express men's voluntary subjection to the rule of the wicked one while they live, and his power to surround death to them, when it comes, with all the terrors of the wages of sin. But as this is a real and terrible sway, so all Scripture represents men as righteously sold under it.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly answers the contradiction: explains in what sense Satan is 'prince/god of this world' (Joh 12:31; Co2 4:4) — a real but limited rule over men's voluntary subjection, not a sovereignty rivaling YHWH's ownership of the earth. The single strongest on-tension harmonization in the gather.

pd_work.resource: Jamieson, Fausset & Brown, Commentary Critical and Explanatory on the Whole Bible (1871), on Matthew 4:8-9 and 2 Corinthians 4:4
pd_work.author: Jamieson, Fausset & Brown
pd_work.note: JFB treats this passage directly, arguing Satan's 'delivered unto me' is 'not wholly false' — a real but deputed, derivative sway over men's voluntary subjection, not a rule rivaling God's sovereignty.

link.title: GotQuestions: How is Satan god of this world (2 Corinthians 4:4)?
link.note: live apologetic treatment: Satan's dominion as god of this world is real but bounded, with God remaining fully sovereign
